rationale: B wins by being a little more ruthless about proof and kill gates, not because it found magic hiding in a canned-water store. Its finance angle says, "Without the first item, do not pitch this," which is exactly the discipline a founder needs before walking into a reporter's inbox. A has the sharper single headline in "The canned water brand that named its store 'Country Club' just earned a B Corp certification," but then tells the founder to "pick one angle and draft a pitch" before the missing proof is closed. That is how decent angles become deleted emails.
gaps_in_A: Unsupported setup masquerades as insight: "B Corp certification belongs to earnest, mission-forward brands in wellness, food, or apparel." Maybe, but the update does not prove that baseline.
The category angle asserts market behavior it has not sourced: "most beverage brands at 120,000 retail doors add more doors, not their own." That may be true, but it is not in the brief.
The next step is premature: "pick one angle and draft a pitch." The set itself admits the strongest hook needs named nonprofit proof and a certification rationale first.
Some beat targeting is still soft: "A brand journalism reporter or sustainability reporter" is closer than "tech journalist," but still too broad for actual media work.
gaps_in_B: The B Corp angle is mislabeled: "Story type: data." This is accountability or ESG credentialing; calling it data muddies the editor promise.
The second headline overstates the facts: "Liquid Death's first store is a merch shop that also sells water." The update says the store sells merch, not that merch leads the business.
The first two angles crowd each other: "Now it wants one of its own" and "a merch shop that also sells water" both orbit the same brand-lab thesis unless merch revenue is material.

This line is decorative precision: "Certification landed this quarter, which ends June 30." The current date supports the calendar inference, but it does not add much to the story and risks sounding lawyerly instead of useful.
